title.en: Force on a conductor, motor, induction and domestic circuits
From electricity to motion and back

text.en: A fan blade turns because current in a magnetic field feels a force, and a generator makes electricity from motion. Both rest on two rules.

A current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field feels a force, largest when the current is perpendicular to the field.
Fleming's left-hand rule: stretch the thumb, forefinger and middle finger at right angles. Forefinger shows the field, middle finger the current and thumb the force.
An electric motor turns electrical energy into mechanical energy using a coil, magnet, commutator and brushes.
Electromagnetic induction: a changing magnetic field through a coil induces a current. Faraday discovered it.
Fleming's right-hand rule gives the direction of the induced current.
A generator converts mechanical energy into electrical energy. AC reverses direction (50 Hz in India) and DC flows in one direction.
Domestic circuits: live (red), neutral (black) and earth (green) wires. Our supply is 220 V.
Safety: the earth wire sends leakage current to the ground, and fuses or circuit breakers prevent overloading and short circuits.

problem.en: Why does an electric motor need a commutator?

text.en: The coil must keep turning in the same direction.
The commutator reverses the current every half turn.
So the force keeps the coil rotating.
